## People hub: schema and permission model

Design doc for the Directus data model behind Layer 2 of `docs/architecture.md` (the CRM / people
hub), per the plan agreed on issue #69. Covers the collections, fields, and permission policies;
deployment and rollout are tracked in the sibling issues (#92-#95) that decompose #69.

### Scope and non-goals

- Models what Clubspot actually gives us: people, their guardian/emergency-contact relationships,
  camp sessions, and registrations. No household grouping — Clubspot has no concept of a household,
  only per-registration guardians and emergency contacts, so that's what the schema keys off.
- Auth identity is deliberately separate from person data — see [Auth identity](#auth-identity)
  below.
- Coach and guardian **portals** (thin clients calling this API) are out of scope; this doc defines
  the roles/policies they'll eventually use, but nothing here provisions their logins. That's #65.

### Collections

**people** — one row per human known to the org: staff, coaches, guardians, participants, emergency
contacts. Roles aren't stored — they're derived from relationships: staff from `directus_user_id` +
Directus role, coach from an `event_staff` row, guardian/emergency contact from a `contacts` row,
participant from a `registrations` row.

No `clubspot_id` here. Clubspot has no stable person record — each registration carries its own
contact data, and one real person can show up as the contact on many registrations. Deduplicating
and collecting those into a single `people` row (by email, most likely) is the identity-resolution
problem #70's sync has to solve; it isn't a field this schema can just copy in.

| Field                     | Type               | Notes                                |
| ------------------------- | ------------------ | ------------------------------------- |
| `id`                      | uuid                | primary key                          |
| `first_name`, `last_name` | string              |                                       |
| `email`, `phone`          | string, nullable    | contact info, not auth               |
| `date_of_birth`           | date, nullable      | required for minors                  |
| `directus_user_id`        | uuid, nullable, unique, FK -> `directus_users.id` | see [Auth identity](#auth-identity) |

**medical_profiles** — one-to-one with `people`, kept as its own collection so its permission policy
can be stricter than a roster-level `people` read (allergies, medications, conditions, physician
contact).

| Field                                    | Type                            | Notes                  |
| ---------------------------------------- | ------------------------------- | ---------------------- |
| `id`                                     | uuid                            | primary key            |
| `person_id`                              | uuid, FK -> `people.id`, unique | one profile per person |
| `allergies`, `medications`, `conditions` | text                            | free-form              |
| `physician_name`, `physician_phone`      | string, nullable                |                        |

**person_relationships** — one join collection for both relationship kinds Clubspot gives us
(guardian and emergency contact), rather than a separate table per type, since the shape is
identical.

| Field               | Type                                   | Notes                                             |
| ------------------- | -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`                | uuid                                   | primary key                                       |
| `related_person_id` | uuid, FK -> `people.id`                | the minor                                         |
| `person_id`         | uuid, FK -> `people.id`                | the guardian or emergency contact                 |
| `relationship_type` | enum (`guardian`, `emergency_contact`) |                                                   |
| `is_primary`        | boolean                                | contact-order hint when a minor has more than one |

**event_staff** — coach/staff assigned to a session; the row a coach's "see my roster" policy keys
off.

| Field        | Type                      | Notes       |
| ------------ | ------------------------- | ----------- |
| `id`         | uuid                      | primary key |
| `person_id`  | uuid, FK -> `people.id`   |             |
| `session_id` | uuid, FK -> `sessions.id` |             |

**sessions** — camp/program sessions, mirrors Clubspot.

| Field                    | Type                     | Notes             |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------ | ----------------- |
| `id`                     | uuid                     | primary key       |
| `name`, `program`        | string                   |                   |
| `start_date`, `end_date` | date                     |                   |
| `clubspot_session_id`    | string, nullable, unique | dedup key for #70 |

**enrollments** — a participant's registration in a session.

| Field                      | Type                                        | Notes                  |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- | ---------------------- |
| `id`                       | uuid                                        | primary key            |
| `person_id`                | uuid, FK -> `people.id`                     | the participant        |
| `session_id`               | uuid, FK -> `sessions.id`                   |                        |
| `status`                   | enum (`confirmed`, `waitlist`, `cancelled`) | same vocabulary as #60 |
| `clubspot_registration_id` | string, nullable, unique                    | dedup key for #70      |

### Auth identity

Auth info does not live on `people`. Directus already has its own identity table — `directus_users`
— with roles, policies, and OIDC `provider`/`external_identifier` fields for linking a Google login.
Reusing it instead of a homegrown field means:

- `people.directus_user_id` is a nullable, unique FK to `directus_users.id`. Set only for people who
  have an actual login: staff now (provisioned directly by an admin); coach/guardian later, once
  #65's account-linking flow provisions or links a `directus_users` row on first OIDC login.
- Directus's own OIDC config does the email-matching (`provider` + `external_identifier` on
  `directus_users`). This schema has no identity/matching logic of its own — it only points `people`
  at the resulting user once one exists.

### Permission model

- **Administrator** — Directus's built-in full-access role.
- **Staff** — authenticates via Directus's native Google OIDC, restricted to Workspace accounts an
  admin has provisioned as Directus users. Full read/write on every collection above, including
  `medical_profiles`. The only role delivered end-to-end by #69/#92-#95.
- **Coach** — defined now so the schema doesn't need reshaping later, but has no way to log in yet
  (needs #65). Policy: read `sessions` / `enrollments` / `people` filtered through `event_staff` for
  their own sessions. No access to `medical_profiles`.
- **Guardian** — same caveat as Coach. Policy: read their own minors' `people` / `medical_profiles` /
  `enrollments`, filtered through `person_relationships` where `relationship_type == 'guardian'`.
- **Emergency contacts get no role or login.** They're informational rows staff can see on a minor's
  record (`person_relationships` where `relationship_type == 'emergency_contact'`), not a portal
  audience.

### Open questions for the applying slice (#95)

- Exact Directus field types (`uuid` vs. Directus's integer PKs) and whether `person_roles` is a
  Directus "tags" interface field or a normalized M2M — pick whichever keeps the permission filters
  simplest when building the real schema snapshot.
- Whether `medical_profiles` needs field-level (not just collection-level) permissions before a
  Guardian role ever actually logs in.

## People hub: schema and permission model

Design doc for the Directus data model behind Layer 2 of `docs/architecture.md` (the CRM / people
hub), per the plan agreed on issue #69. Covers the collections, fields, and permission policies;
deployment and rollout are tracked in the sibling issues (#92-#95) that decompose #69.

### Scope and non-goals

- Models what Clubspot actually gives us: people, their guardian/emergency-contact relationships,
  camp sessions, and registrations. No household grouping — Clubspot has no concept of a household,
  only per-registration guardians and emergency contacts, so that's what the schema keys off.
- Auth identity is deliberately separate from person data — see [Auth identity](#auth-identity)
  below.
- Coach and guardian **portals** (thin clients calling this API) are out of scope; this doc defines
  the roles/policies they'll eventually use, but nothing here provisions their logins. That's #65.

### Collections

**people** — one row per human known to the org: staff, coaches, guardians, participants, emergency
contacts. Roles aren't stored — they're derived from relationships: staff from `directus_user_id` +
Directus role, coach from an `event_staff` row, guardian/emergency contact from a `contacts` row,
participant from a `registrations` row.

No `clubspot_id` here. Clubspot has no stable person record — each registration carries its own
contact data, and one real person can show up as the contact on many registrations. Deduplicating
and collecting those into a single `people` row (by email, most likely) is the identity-resolution
problem #70's sync has to solve; it isn't a field this schema can just copy in.

| Field                     | Type               | Notes                                |
| ------------------------- | ------------------ | ------------------------------------- |
| `id`                      | uuid                | primary key                          |
| `first_name`, `last_name` | string              |                                       |
| `email`, `phone`          | string, nullable    | contact info, not auth               |
| `date_of_birth`           | date, nullable      | required for minors                  |
| `directus_user_id`        | uuid, nullable, unique, FK -> `directus_users.id` | see [Auth identity](#auth-identity) |

**medical_profiles** — one-to-one with `people`, kept as its own collection so its permission policy
can be stricter than a roster-level `people` read (allergies, medications, conditions, physician
contact).

| Field                                     | Type                        | Notes                                              |
| ------------------------------------------ | --------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| `person_id`                                | uuid, PK, FK -> `people.id` | one profile per person, so `person_id` is the key |
| `allergies`, `medications`, `conditions`  | text                        | free-form                                          |
| `physician_name`, `physician_phone`       | string, nullable            |                                                     |

**contacts** — one join collection for both relationship kinds Clubspot gives us (guardian and
emergency contact), rather than a separate table per type, since the shape is identical. Other
relationship kinds, if they're ever needed, get their own dedicated table rather than growing this
one's `relationship_type` enum.

| Field               | Type                                   | Notes                                    |
| ------------------- | --------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| `id`                | uuid                                    | primary key                              |
| `related_person_id` | uuid, FK -> `people.id`                 | the minor                                |
| `person_id`         | uuid, FK -> `people.id`                 | the guardian or emergency contact        |
| `relationship_type` | enum (`guardian`, `emergency_contact`)  |                                           |
| `contact_order`     | integer                                 | call order when a minor has more than one |

**event_staff** — coach/staff assigned to a session. This is the row that makes someone a "coach"
(derived, not stored on `people`) — not used to scope roster permissions yet, see
[Permission model](#permission-model).

| Field        | Type                      | Notes       |
| ------------ | ------------------------- | ----------- |
| `id`         | uuid                      | primary key |
| `person_id`  | uuid, FK -> `people.id`   |             |
| `session_id` | uuid, FK -> `sessions.id` |             |

**sessions** — camp/program sessions, mirrors Clubspot.

| Field                    | Type                     | Notes             |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------ | ----------------- |
| `id`                     | uuid                     | primary key       |
| `name`, `program`        | string                   |                   |
| `start_date`, `end_date` | date                     |                   |
| `clubspot_session_id`    | string, nullable, unique | dedup key for #70 |

**enrollments** — a participant's registration in a session.

| Field                      | Type                                        | Notes                  |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- | ---------------------- |
| `id`                       | uuid                                        | primary key            |
| `person_id`                | uuid, FK -> `people.id`                     | the participant        |
| `session_id`               | uuid, FK -> `sessions.id`                   |                        |
| `status`                   | enum (`confirmed`, `waitlist`, `cancelled`) | same vocabulary as #60 |
| `clubspot_registration_id` | string, nullable, unique                    | dedup key for #70      |

### Auth identity

Auth info does not live on `people`. Directus already has its own identity table — `directus_users`
— with roles, policies, and OIDC `provider`/`external_identifier` fields for linking a Google login.
Reusing it instead of a homegrown field means:

- `people.directus_user_id` is a nullable, unique FK to `directus_users.id`. Set only for people who
  have an actual login: staff now (provisioned directly by an admin); coach/guardian later, once
  #65's account-linking flow provisions or links a `directus_users` row on first OIDC login.
- Directus's own OIDC config does the email-matching (`provider` + `external_identifier` on
  `directus_users`). This schema has no identity/matching logic of its own — it only points `people`
  at the resulting user once one exists.

### Permission model

- **Administrator** — Directus's built-in full-access role.
- **Staff** — authenticates via Directus's native Google OIDC, restricted to Workspace accounts an
  admin has provisioned as Directus users. Full read/write on every collection above, including
  `medical_profiles`. The only role delivered end-to-end by #69/#92-#95.
- **Coach** — defined now so the schema doesn't need reshaping later, but has no way to log in yet
  (needs #65). Policy: read `sessions` / `enrollments` / `people` filtered through `event_staff` for
  their own sessions. No access to `medical_profiles`.
- **Guardian** — same caveat as Coach. Policy: read their own minors' `people` / `medical_profiles` /
  `enrollments`, filtered through `person_relationships` where `relationship_type == 'guardian'`.
- **Emergency contacts get no role or login.** They're informational rows staff can see on a minor's
  record (`person_relationships` where `relationship_type == 'emergency_contact'`), not a portal
  audience.

### Open questions for the applying slice (#95)

- Exact Directus field types (`uuid` vs. Directus's integer PKs) and whether `person_roles` is a
  Directus "tags" interface field or a normalized M2M — pick whichever keeps the permission filters
  simplest when building the real schema snapshot.
- Whether `medical_profiles` needs field-level (not just collection-level) permissions before a
  Guardian role ever actually logs in.

## People hub: schema and permission model

Design doc for the Directus data model behind Layer 2 of `docs/architecture.md` (the CRM / people
hub), per the plan agreed on issue #69. Covers the collections, fields, and permission policies;
deployment and rollout are tracked in the sibling issues (#92-#95) that decompose #69.

### Scope and non-goals

- Models what Clubspot actually gives us: people, their guardian/emergency-contact relationships,
  camp sessions, and registrations. No household grouping — Clubspot has no concept of a household,
  only per-registration guardians and emergency contacts, so that's what the schema keys off.
- Auth identity is deliberately separate from person data — see [Auth identity](#auth-identity)
  below.
- Coach and guardian **portals** (thin clients calling this API) are out of scope; this doc defines
  the roles/policies they'll eventually use, but nothing here provisions their logins. That's #65.

### Collections

**people** — one row per human known to the org: staff, coaches, guardians, participants, emergency
contacts. Roles aren't stored — they're derived from relationships: staff from `directus_user_id` +
Directus role, coach from an `event_staff` row, guardian/emergency contact from a `contacts` row,
participant from a `registrations` row.

No `clubspot_id` here. Clubspot has no stable person record — each registration carries its own
contact data, and one real person can show up as the contact on many registrations. Deduplicating
and collecting those into a single `people` row (by email, most likely) is the identity-resolution
problem #70's sync has to solve; it isn't a field this schema can just copy in.

| Field                     | Type               | Notes                                |
| ------------------------- | ------------------ | ------------------------------------- |
| `id`                      | uuid                | primary key                          |
| `first_name`, `last_name` | string              |                                       |
| `email`, `phone`          | string, nullable    | contact info, not auth               |
| `date_of_birth`           | date, nullable      | required for minors                  |
| `directus_user_id`        | uuid, nullable, unique, FK -> `directus_users.id` | see [Auth identity](#auth-identity) |

**medical_profiles** — one-to-one with `people`, kept as its own collection so its permission policy
can be stricter than a roster-level `people` read (allergies, medications, conditions, physician
contact).

| Field                                     | Type                        | Notes                                              |
| ------------------------------------------ | --------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| `person_id`                                | uuid, PK, FK -> `people.id` | one profile per person, so `person_id` is the key |
| `allergies`, `medications`, `conditions`  | text                        | free-form                                          |
| `physician_name`, `physician_phone`       | string, nullable            |                                                     |

**contacts** — one join collection for both relationship kinds Clubspot gives us (guardian and
emergency contact), rather than a separate table per type, since the shape is identical. Other
relationship kinds, if they're ever needed, get their own dedicated table rather than growing this
one's `relationship_type` enum.

| Field               | Type                                   | Notes                                    |
| ------------------- | --------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| `id`                | uuid                                    | primary key                              |
| `related_person_id` | uuid, FK -> `people.id`                 | the minor                                |
| `person_id`         | uuid, FK -> `people.id`                 | the guardian or emergency contact        |
| `relationship_type` | enum (`guardian`, `emergency_contact`)  |                                           |
| `contact_order`     | integer                                 | call order when a minor has more than one |

**event_staff** — coach/staff assigned to a session. This is the row that makes someone a "coach"
(derived, not stored on `people`) — not used to scope roster permissions yet, see
[Permission model](#permission-model).

| Field        | Type                      | Notes       |
| ------------ | ------------------------- | ----------- |
| `id`         | uuid                      | primary key |
| `person_id`  | uuid, FK -> `people.id`   |             |
| `session_id` | uuid, FK -> `sessions.id` |             |

**sessions** — camp/program sessions, mirrors Clubspot.

| Field                    | Type                     | Notes             |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------ | ----------------- |
| `id`                     | uuid                     | primary key       |
| `name`, `program`        | string                   |                   |
| `start_date`, `end_date` | date                     |                   |
| `clubspot_session_id`    | string, nullable, unique | dedup key for #70 |

**registrations** — a participant's registration in a session (Clubspot's own term — matched here
rather than "enrollment").

| Field                      | Type                                        | Notes                  |
| -------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- | ------------------------ |
| `id`                       | uuid                                        | primary key            |
| `person_id`                | uuid, FK -> `people.id`                     | the participant        |
| `session_id`               | uuid, FK -> `sessions.id`                   |                        |
| `status`                   | enum (`confirmed`, `waitlist`, `cancelled`) | same vocabulary as #60 |
| `clubspot_registration_id` | string, nullable, unique                    | dedup key for #70      |

### Auth identity

Auth info does not live on `people`. Directus already has its own identity table — `directus_users`
— with roles, policies, and OIDC `provider`/`external_identifier` fields for linking a Google login.
Reusing it instead of a homegrown field means:

- `people.directus_user_id` is a nullable, unique FK to `directus_users.id`. Set only for people who
  have an actual login: staff now (provisioned directly by an admin); coach/guardian later, once
  #65's account-linking flow provisions or links a `directus_users` row on first OIDC login.
- Directus's own OIDC config does the email-matching (`provider` + `external_identifier` on
  `directus_users`). This schema has no identity/matching logic of its own — it only points `people`
  at the resulting user once one exists.

### Permission model

- **Administrator** — Directus's built-in full-access role.
- **Staff** — authenticates via Directus's native Google OIDC, restricted to Workspace accounts an
  admin has provisioned as Directus users. Full read/write on every collection above, including
  `medical_profiles`. The only role delivered end-to-end by #69/#92-#95.
- **Coach** — defined now so the schema doesn't need reshaping later, but has no way to log in yet
  (needs #65). Policy: read `sessions` / `enrollments` / `people` filtered through `event_staff` for
  their own sessions. No access to `medical_profiles`.
- **Guardian** — same caveat as Coach. Policy: read their own minors' `people` / `medical_profiles` /
  `enrollments`, filtered through `person_relationships` where `relationship_type == 'guardian'`.
- **Emergency contacts get no role or login.** They're informational rows staff can see on a minor's
  record (`person_relationships` where `relationship_type == 'emergency_contact'`), not a portal
  audience.

### Open questions for the applying slice (#95)

- Exact Directus field types (`uuid` vs. Directus's integer PKs) and whether `person_roles` is a
  Directus "tags" interface field or a normalized M2M — pick whichever keeps the permission filters
  simplest when building the real schema snapshot.
- Whether `medical_profiles` needs field-level (not just collection-level) permissions before a
  Guardian role ever actually logs in.

## People hub: schema and permission model

Design doc for the Directus data model behind Layer 2 of `docs/architecture.md` (the CRM / people
hub), per the plan agreed on issue #69. Covers the collections, fields, and permission policies;
deployment and rollout are tracked in the sibling issues (#92-#95) that decompose #69.

### Scope and non-goals

- Models what Clubspot actually gives us: people, their guardian/emergency-contact relationships,
  camp sessions, and registrations. No household grouping — Clubspot has no concept of a household,
  only per-registration guardians and emergency contacts, so that's what the schema keys off.
- Auth identity is deliberately separate from person data — see [Auth identity](#auth-identity)
  below.
- Coach and guardian **portals** (thin clients calling this API) are out of scope; this doc defines
  the roles/policies they'll eventually use, but nothing here provisions their logins. That's #65.

### Collections

**people** — one row per human known to the org: staff, coaches, guardians, participants, emergency
contacts. Roles aren't stored — they're derived from relationships: staff from `directus_user_id` +
Directus role, coach from an `event_staff` row, guardian/emergency contact from a `contacts` row,
participant from a `registrations` row.

No `clubspot_id` here. Clubspot has no stable person record — each registration carries its own
contact data, and one real person can show up as the contact on many registrations. Deduplicating
and collecting those into a single `people` row (by email, most likely) is the identity-resolution
problem #70's sync has to solve; it isn't a field this schema can just copy in.

| Field                     | Type               | Notes                                |
| ------------------------- | ------------------ | ------------------------------------- |
| `id`                      | uuid                | primary key                          |
| `first_name`, `last_name` | string              |                                       |
| `email`, `phone`          | string, nullable    | contact info, not auth               |
| `date_of_birth`           | date, nullable      | required for minors                  |
| `directus_user_id`        | uuid, nullable, unique, FK -> `directus_users.id` | see [Auth identity](#auth-identity) |

**medical_profiles** — one-to-one with `people`, kept as its own collection so its permission policy
can be stricter than a roster-level `people` read (allergies, medications, conditions, physician
contact).

| Field                                     | Type                        | Notes                                              |
| ------------------------------------------ | --------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| `person_id`                                | uuid, PK, FK -> `people.id` | one profile per person, so `person_id` is the key |
| `allergies`, `medications`, `conditions`  | text                        | free-form                                          |
| `physician_name`, `physician_phone`       | string, nullable            |                                                     |

**contacts** — one join collection for both relationship kinds Clubspot gives us (guardian and
emergency contact), rather than a separate table per type, since the shape is identical. Other
relationship kinds, if they're ever needed, get their own dedicated table rather than growing this
one's `relationship_type` enum.

| Field               | Type                                   | Notes                                    |
| ------------------- | --------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| `id`                | uuid                                    | primary key                              |
| `related_person_id` | uuid, FK -> `people.id`                 | the minor                                |
| `person_id`         | uuid, FK -> `people.id`                 | the guardian or emergency contact        |
| `relationship_type` | enum (`guardian`, `emergency_contact`)  |                                           |
| `contact_order`     | integer                                 | call order when a minor has more than one |

**event_staff** — coach/staff assigned to a session. This is the row that makes someone a "coach"
(derived, not stored on `people`) — not used to scope roster permissions yet, see
[Permission model](#permission-model).

| Field        | Type                      | Notes       |
| ------------ | ------------------------- | ----------- |
| `id`         | uuid                      | primary key |
| `person_id`  | uuid, FK -> `people.id`   |             |
| `session_id` | uuid, FK -> `sessions.id` |             |

**sessions** — camp/program sessions, mirrors Clubspot.

| Field                    | Type                     | Notes             |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------ | ----------------- |
| `id`                     | uuid                     | primary key       |
| `name`, `program`        | string                   |                   |
| `start_date`, `end_date` | date                     |                   |
| `clubspot_session_id`    | string, nullable, unique | dedup key for #70 |

**registrations** — a participant's registration in a session (Clubspot's own term — matched here
rather than "enrollment").

| Field                      | Type                                        | Notes                  |
| -------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- | ------------------------ |
| `id`                       | uuid                                        | primary key            |
| `person_id`                | uuid, FK -> `people.id`                     | the participant        |
| `session_id`               | uuid, FK -> `sessions.id`                   |                        |
| `status`                   | enum (`confirmed`, `waitlist`, `cancelled`) | same vocabulary as #60 |
| `clubspot_registration_id` | string, nullable, unique                    | dedup key for #70      |

### Auth identity

Auth info does not live on `people`. Directus already has its own identity table — `directus_users`
— with roles, policies, and OIDC `provider`/`external_identifier` fields for linking a Google login.
Reusing it instead of a homegrown field means:

- `people.directus_user_id` is a nullable, unique FK to `directus_users.id`. Set only for people who
  have an actual login: staff now (provisioned directly by an admin); coach/guardian later, once
  #65's account-linking flow provisions or links a `directus_users` row on first OIDC login.
- Directus's own OIDC config does the email-matching (`provider` + `external_identifier` on
  `directus_users`). This schema has no identity/matching logic of its own — it only points `people`
  at the resulting user once one exists.

### Permission model

- **Administrator** — Directus's built-in full-access role.
- **Staff** — authenticates via Directus's native Google OIDC, restricted to Workspace accounts an
  admin has provisioned as Directus users. Full read/write on every collection above, including
  `medical_profiles`. The only role delivered end-to-end by #69/#92-#95.
- **Coach** — defined now so the schema doesn't need reshaping later, but has no way to log in yet
  (needs #65). KISS for now: any authenticated Directus user can read `sessions` / `registrations` /
  `people` roster fields (no `medical_profiles`) — scoping a coach to only their own sessions via
  `event_staff` is a follow-up, not built here.
- **Guardian** — same login caveat as Coach. Policy: read their own minors' `people` /
  `medical_profiles` / `registrations`, filtered through `contacts` where
  `relationship_type == 'guardian'`. This scoping isn't KISS'd away like the coach roster case above
  — it's the medical-data boundary the whole design doc exists to get right.
- **Emergency contacts get no role or login.** They're informational rows staff can see on a minor's
  record (`contacts` where `relationship_type == 'emergency_contact'`), not a portal audience.

### Open questions for the applying slice (#95)

- Exact Directus field types (`uuid` vs. Directus's integer PKs) for every collection above — pick
  whichever keeps the permission filters simplest when building the real schema snapshot.
- Whether `medical_profiles` needs field-level (not just collection-level) permissions before a
  Guardian role ever actually logs in.
- The actual person-dedup rule #70 will use (email match, most likely, with a manual merge path for
  the rest) — out of scope here, but the schema above assumes one exists.

  the rest) — out of scope here, but the schema above assumes one exists.

  (`CampClass`) concept is named for, but not modeled by, this schema — see the `programs`/`sessions`
  note below.
- Auth identity is deliberately separate from person data — see [Auth identity](#auth-identity)
  below.
- Coach and guardian **portals** (thin clients calling this API) are out of scope; this doc defines
  the roles/policies they'll eventually use, but nothing here provisions their logins. That's #65.

### Collections

**people** — one row per human known to the org: staff, coaches, guardians, participants, emergency
contacts. Roles aren't stored — they're derived from relationships: staff from `directus_user_id` +
Directus role, coach from an `event_staff` row, guardian/emergency contact from a `contacts` row,
participant from a `registrations` row.

No `clubspot_id` here. Clubspot has no stable person record — each registration carries its own
contact data, and one real person can show up as the contact on many registrations. Deduplicating
and collecting those into a single `people` row (by email, most likely) is the identity-resolution
problem #70's sync has to solve; it isn't a field this schema can just copy in.

| Field                     | Type                                              | Notes                               |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------- |
| `id`                      | uuid                                              | primary key                         |
| `first_name`, `last_name` | string                                            |                                     |
| `email`, `phone`          | string, nullable                                  | contact info, not auth              |
| `date_of_birth`           | date, nullable                                    | required for minors                 |
| `directus_user_id`        | uuid, nullable, unique, FK -> `directus_users.id` | see [Auth identity](#auth-identity) |

**medical_profiles** — one-to-one with `people`, kept as its own collection so its permission policy
can be stricter than a roster-level `people` read (allergies, medications, conditions, physician
contact).

| Field                                    | Type                        | Notes                                             |
| ---------------------------------------- | --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `person_id`                              | uuid, PK, FK -> `people.id` | one profile per person, so `person_id` is the key |
| `allergies`, `medications`, `conditions` | text                        | free-form                                         |
| `physician_name`, `physician_phone`      | string, nullable            |                                                   |

**contacts** — one join collection for both relationship kinds Clubspot gives us (guardian and
emergency contact), rather than a separate table per type, since the shape is identical. Other
relationship kinds, if they're ever needed, get their own dedicated table rather than growing this
one's `relationship_type` enum.

Like `people`, these rows have no Clubspot id of their own to key off — Clubspot doesn't model a
guardian/emergency contact as a linked record, just flat strings on the participant
(`parentGuardianName`/`_secondary`, `emergencyContact`/`emergencyRelationship`). `contact_order`
is what recovers Clubspot's primary-vs-secondary guardian distinction once #70 turns those flat
fields into rows here.

| Field               | Type                                   | Notes                                     |
| ------------------- | -------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| `id`                | uuid                                   | primary key                               |
| `related_person_id` | uuid, FK -> `people.id`                | the minor                                 |
| `person_id`         | uuid, FK -> `people.id`                | the guardian or emergency contact         |
| `relationship_type` | enum (`guardian`, `emergency_contact`) |                                           |
| `contact_order`     | integer                                | call order when a minor has more than one |

**event_staff** — coach/staff assigned to a session. This is the row that makes someone a "coach"
(derived, not stored on `people`) — not used to scope roster permissions yet, see
[Permission model](#permission-model).

| Field        | Type                      | Notes       |
| ------------ | ------------------------- | ----------- |
| `id`         | uuid                      | primary key |
| `person_id`  | uuid, FK -> `people.id`   |             |
| `session_id` | uuid, FK -> `sessions.id` |             |

**programs** — matches org/Clubspot terminology: a program is what CYC calls a `Camp` in Clubspot
(e.g. "Youth Camp", "LTS Weekday", "ILCA Race Team") — the thing on the website you sign up for.

| Field              | Type                     | Notes             |
| ------------------ | ------------------------ | ----------------- |
| `id`               | uuid                     | primary key       |
| `name`             | string                   |                   |
| `clubspot_camp_id` | string, nullable, unique | dedup key for #70 |

**sessions** — a dated instance of a program (Clubspot's `CampSession`).

| Field                    | Type                      | Notes             |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------- | ----------------- |
| `id`                     | uuid                      | primary key       |
| `program_id`             | uuid, FK -> `programs.id` |                   |
| `start_date`, `end_date` | date                      |                   |
| `clubspot_session_id`    | string, nullable, unique  | dedup key for #70 |

Clubspot also has **classes** (`CampClass` — an age/skill subdivision within a program, e.g.
"Beginner" vs. "Advanced") that this schema doesn't model yet. The people hub's own needs (roster,
permissions) only require session granularity; `programs`/`sessions` are named so a `classes`
collection can slot in later — FK'd the same way as `sessions` — without a rename. Don't build it
speculatively now; a later issue can add it when something actually needs class-level data (the
financial-model-replacement app most likely will).

**registrations** — a participant's registration in a session (Clubspot's own term — matched here
rather than "enrollment"). A single Clubspot registration can span multiple sessions (and classes);
#70's sync fans that out into one `registrations` row per session.

| Field                      | Type                                        | Notes                  |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- | ---------------------- |
| `id`                       | uuid                                        | primary key            |
| `person_id`                | uuid, FK -> `people.id`                     | the participant        |
| `session_id`               | uuid, FK -> `sessions.id`                   |                        |
| `status`                   | enum (`confirmed`, `waitlist`, `cancelled`) | same vocabulary as #60 |
| `clubspot_registration_id` | string, nullable, unique                    | dedup key for #70      |

### Auth identity

Auth info does not live on `people`. Directus already has its own identity table — `directus_users`
— with roles, policies, and OIDC `provider`/`external_identifier` fields for linking a Google login.
Reusing it instead of a homegrown field means:

- `people.directus_user_id` is a nullable, unique FK to `directus_users.id`. Set only for people who
  have an actual login: staff now (provisioned directly by an admin); coach/guardian later, once
  #65's account-linking flow provisions or links a `directus_users` row on first OIDC login.
- Directus's own OIDC config does the email-matching (`provider` + `external_identifier` on
  `directus_users`). This schema has no identity/matching logic of its own — it only points `people`
  at the resulting user once one exists.

### Permission model

- **Administrator** — Directus's built-in full-access role.
- **Staff** — authenticates via Directus's native Google OIDC, restricted to Workspace accounts an
  admin has provisioned as Directus users. Full read/write on every collection above, including
  `medical_profiles`. The only role delivered end-to-end by #69/#92-#95.
- **Coach** — defined now so the schema doesn't need reshaping later, but has no way to log in yet
  (needs #65). KISS for now: any authenticated Directus user can read `sessions` / `registrations` /
  `people` roster fields (no `medical_profiles`) — scoping a coach to only their own sessions via
  `event_staff` is a follow-up, not built here.
- **Guardian** — same login caveat as Coach. Policy: read their own minors' `people` /
  `medical_profiles` / `registrations`, filtered through `contacts` where
  `relationship_type == 'guardian'`. This scoping isn't KISS'd away like the coach roster case above
  — it's the medical-data boundary the whole design doc exists to get right.
- **Emergency contacts get no role or login.** They're informational rows staff can see on a minor's
  record (`contacts` where `relationship_type == 'emergency_contact'`), not a portal audience.

### Open questions for the applying slice (#95)

- Exact Directus field types (`uuid` vs. Directus's integer PKs) for every collection above — pick
  whichever keeps the permission filters simplest when building the real schema snapshot.
- Whether `medical_profiles` needs field-level (not just collection-level) permissions before a
  Guardian role ever actually logs in.
- The actual person-dedup rule #70 will use (email match, most likely, with a manual merge path for
  the rest) — out of scope here, but the schema above assumes one exists.

The spreadsheet's hierarchy is Program category → Program (e.g. "Youth", "LTS Weekday") → Session (a dated week, or a weekly meeting for recurring programs). content.thinking:
This confirms ParticipantsReport is likely exactly what builds the "participants spreadsheet" the user's referencing, with its point-in-time snapshot structure of one row per registration and session-join, which matches the flattened format the user says loses history when updates occur.

Since the user gave an actual live Google Sheet URL, I should fetch it to confirm the match and check for extra tabs, pivot tables, or manual filters, plus see real examples of guardian fields to reason about the multi-registration-to-one-guardian dedup problem — I'll fork this since it's likely large.

Now I want to work through the actual schema changes to propose. First, classes should be built now rather than deferred: I'm adding a CampClass collection with an id, a program or session foreign key, name, and clubspot_class_id, matching the real model where a CampClass belongs to a Program and a CampSession can offer an array of CampClasses, and where EntryCap references both a CampClass and optionally a CampSession, implying capacity is scoped per class per session.

The RegistrationCampSession join (matching the "Session Join Id" column in the report) is really the connector between a registration, a specific class, and a specific session — so registrations aren't just person+session, they're person+session+class, and a multi-week registration fans out into one row per session, each tied to a specific class.

So I should add a **classes** collection scoped to program with a clubspot ID, and update **registrations** to have both `session_id` and `class_id` FKs, since one row = one (person, session, class) triple matching Clubspot's session join concept. That means `clubspot_registration_id` alone won't be unique per row anymore — I need a `clubspot_session_join_id` as the true unique dedup key, while `clubspot_registration_id` becomes a non-unique grouping reference shared across multiple rows.

Now I need to address change tracking for registrations, since status and payment details shift over time and a single point-in-time row loses that history. I'm weighing two approaches: an event log table recording each transition with timestamps and old/new values, versus a slowly-changing-dimension pattern that preserves prior versions while keeping a current row.

I'm also considering whether Directus's built-in revisions/activity log — which automatically tracks every create/update per item — could cover this need out of the box rather than requiring a custom history table, though that mechanism is really geared toward manual admin edits rather than tracking the actual source of registration changes over time.

Since generic revision blobs are hard to query for clean status timelines, and the user flagged tracking as explicitly important, I'm leaning toward a dedicated status history table as first-class schema — giving clean reporting like average days-to-confirmation or waitlist churn, which would also feed into the financial-model app later. I'm starting to sketch out what that events table should look like.

Since a parent might change their email between one registration and another, `people.email` shouldn't just be a flat overwritten field — I need to track which registration last supplied a given value and when, so the sync can prefer the most recent source while retaining history for staff to audit ("this email came from June's registration, this other one from September's"). This calls for the same event/history pattern as registration status changes, but applied to person field values sourced from registrations, likely via a generic history collection tracking field provenance over time.

The alternative would be to compute `people.email` entirely on the fly from history rather than storing it directly, but keeping a simple current-value field alongside the history table is better for performance and staff usability in Directus.

The same pattern likely applies beyond contact fields — guardian info on `contacts` rows can shift across registrations too, and registration status changes deserve their own first-class log. So I'm leaning toward two mechanisms: a dedicated `registration_status_history` table for status transitions, plus a more general provenance/history table that tracks which registration sourced each changed field value.

Since the user explicitly wants real change tracking rather than just "latest known source," a lightweight current-source pointer alone won't satisfy the requirement — an actual history log is needed for at least the fields that matter (contact details and registration status).

Given this touches the core schema design, I'm designing a single generic table to handle both registration status changes and person contact-field changes, since the structure is the same in each case: which record, which field, what value, sourced from which registration, and observed at what time. I'm sketching that schema out as a generic history/provenance table with columns for subject collection, subject id, field name, value, and source registration reference.

Adding remaining columns for observed_at and recorded_at rounds out the ledger design, and I'm noting this generic event-log approach avoids needing separate history tables per field or collection, though it's less strongly typed. Directus actually supports exactly this kind of polymorphic reference natively through its Many-to-Any relation type, which seems like a good fit for modeling subject_collection/subject_id.

Given I'm mid-review on an already sizable PR, I think the right sequencing is: first address the concrete "build classes now" comment by implementing the classes collection plus the registrations.class_id and clubspot_session_join_id fixes, then separately fold in the change-tracking and provenance design — since that request came as a new chat message rather than a PR review comment, and the design doc PR hasn't merged yet, it makes sense to expand it with new "Change tracking" and "Data provenance" sections rather than opening something separate. Before finalizing, I want to pull the participants spreadsheet through the fork to validate the real data against this schema.

content.thinking:
While waiting, I'm sketching the schema changes: adding a classes collection, updating registrations to reference session_id and class_id while fixing the clubspot_registration_id uniqueness issue, and adding a category field to programs based on what I saw in the file metadata.

For tracking registration status changes over time, I'm designing a focused append-only registration_status_events table rather than a generic solution—capturing status, when Clubspot recorded the change, and when the sync wrote the row so I can gauge sync latency. Now I'm thinking through how to capture provenance for person/contact data fields sourced from registrations.

Since contacts link to people via person_id, a guardian's email/phone is really just their own people.email/phone, so provenance narrows down to a handful of fields on the people table: email, phone, first_name, last_name (names matter too, since variants like "Bob" vs "Robert" can appear across registrations). This points toward a generic person_field_history table keyed by person_id and a field enum covering these attributes.

Each history row would store the value, an optional source_registration_id linking to whichever registration supplied it, an observed_at timestamp reflecting when that registration was submitted, and a recorded_at timestamp for when the sync process wrote it. The flat people.email/phone fields would then always reflect the "most recent observed_at wins" value, while the history table preserves the full trail so staff can resolve conflicts like differing emails across siblings' registrations. Noticing this mirrors the registration_status_events pattern of value+source+timestamp logs, I'm considering generalizing into a single polymorphic change_log collection using Directus's M2A relation type instead of maintaining separate history tables.

But I'm weighing that against the added complexity of M2A joins in Directus permissions — filtering something like "guardian sees only their own minor's history" gets messier against a polymorphic table. Given the reviewer's stated preference for KISS (they already asked me to simplify Coach permissions), I'll lean toward proposing the two explicitly-typed tables since they're more directly filterable, while still mentioning the polymorphic generalization as an option worth noting.

I'm also reconsidering whether `medical_profiles` should get similar historical tracking, since allergy info also comes from registrations and can conflict across siblings' forms over time. I'll flag this as a natural future extension rather than building it now, to avoid scope creep beyond what was actually asked.

Turning to `contacts` rows, I'm weighing whether guardian linkage changes (like a different secondary guardian appearing after a divorce or remarriage) need their own history tracking too, versus treating a genuinely different guardian as a distinct case entirely.

I think contacts are naturally append-mostly — a person either is or isn't linked as a guardian, so replacement means adding or deactivating a row rather than logging field history. Instead of a full history table, a lightweight `observed_at`/`last_confirmed_at` timestamp directly on `contacts` would let staff see when a guardian linkage was last confirmed by a registration, which feels like the right-sized addition here.

Extending this same logic to registrations, `registrations.status` should stay a cached "current status" like people.email, with `registration_status_events` capturing the full history — consistent with the pattern elsewhere. I'm feeling good about the overall design now and want to wait for the fork results to confirm the Category field and check for real drift examples before writing it all up, while also fixing the classes/registrations linkage and reconsidering whether the granular session+class row should be renamed to something like `registration_sessions` to avoid confusion with "registration" as a whole.

That distinction actually matters more than I thought: a real registration (one per `clubspot_registration_id`) may span multiple sessions/classes, so I should model a parent `registrations` table and a child `registration_sessions`/`session_registrations` table for each session+class join, mirroring Clubspot's actual Registration -> RegistrationCampSession structure. Under this model, `registration_status_events` would hang off the parent Registration rather than the session join, since status fields like "confirmed"/"waitlist"/"cancelled" appear to live on the Registration attributes themselves rather than the session join object — I want to double check this against the type definitions.

Let me check the full RegistrationCampSessionAttributes definition to settle this.

This confirms it — the `RegistrationCampSession` join object already has its own `waitlist_updates` array tracking reason, timestamp, waitlist status, and waitlist number, meaning Clubspot's own data model already maintains a change-history log for waitlist status.

My current sync only surfaces the latest computed status and throws that array away, so I should instead sync `waitlist_updates` into our own status-events table to inherit Clubspot's exact historical timestamps rather than inferring history from our polling cadence. This also confirms registration granularity should live at the RegistrationCampSession level — session_id + class_id + status + waitlist history — not at a coarser registration level.

I don't need a separate parent Registration entity since billing is out of scope for the people-hub, so I'll keep `clubspot_registration_id` as a non-unique grouping key and use `clubspot_session_join_id` as the true per-row unique key mirroring RegistrationCampSession's id. The status-events table should capture both the waitlist_updates equivalent and general status transitions, possibly renamed to `registration_status_history` to match Clubspot's real field naming.

I'm noting that #70's sync should backfill this table directly from Clubspot's own historical `waitlist_updates` array rather than only recording transitions observed between polls, since that gives accurate timestamps. I want to hold off finalizing everything until the fork reports back on the actual spreadsheet, in case it surfaces things like Category values or contact-drift examples — I'll keep reasoning and drafting in the meantime.

I'm also turning to the `classes` collection: CampClass belongs directly to a Camp (not a session), and there may be a self-referential `subclassesArray` field that's still unconfirmed, along with an EntryCap reference to sort out.

Now I realize a class references both its own object and a specific CampSession object, meaning capacity is tracked per-session — so a class is really a program-level concept ("Beginner", "Advanced") that gets offered within particular sessions, making `classes` belong to `programs` rather than `sessions`. This means `CampSession.campClassesArray` forms a many-to-many relationship between sessions and classes, useful for display purposes ("this session offers Beginner and Advanced") even though the people-hub's core roster/registration needs already pin the exact session+class combo through the registration row itself.

Since the reviewer specifically flagged that "registrations are for session + class," I'm settling on adding a `classes` table (id, program_id FK, name, clubspot_class_id nullable/unique) and a `class_id` FK on `registrations` — likely required rather than nullable, since existing camp attributes suggest every session-join always has an assigned class, consistent with report headers always including a "Class" column.

I'm intentionally excluding a session<->class capacity M2M table (EntryCap) since that's future financial-model territory, not people-hub scope. input.new_string:
**programs** — matches org/Clubspot terminology: a program is what CYC calls a `Camp` in Clubspot
(e.g. "Youth Camp", "LTS Weekday", "ILCA Race Team") — the thing on the website you sign up for.

| Field              | Type                     | Notes                                          |
| ------------------- | ------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `id`                | uuid                     | primary key                                    |
| `name`              | string                   |                                                 |
| `category`          | string, nullable         | Clubspot's own grouping (e.g. "Summer Camp", "Junior Racing", "Adult Sailing") |
| `clubspot_camp_id`  | string, nullable, unique | dedup key for #70                              |

**sessions** — a dated instance of a program (Clubspot's `CampSession`).

| Field                    | Type                      | Notes             |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------- | ----------------- |
| `id`                     | uuid                      | primary key       |
| `program_id`             | uuid, FK -> `programs.id` |                   |
| `start_date`, `end_date` | date                      |                   |
| `clubspot_session_id`    | string, nullable, unique  | dedup key for #70 |

**classes** — an age/skill subdivision within a program (Clubspot's `CampClass`, e.g. "Beginner" vs.
"Advanced"). Modeled now, not deferred: a registration is for a specific session *and* class, and
#70's sync needs somewhere to put that — see `registrations` below.

| Field                | Type                      | Notes             |
| --------------------- | ------------------------- | ----------------- |
| `id`                  | uuid                      | primary key       |
| `program_id`          | uuid, FK -> `programs.id` | a class belongs to the program, independent of which sessions offer it |
| `name`                | string                   |                   |
| `clubspot_class_id`   | string, nullable, unique | dedup key for #70 |

Not modeled: which classes a given session offers (Clubspot's `CampSession.campClassesArray`) or
per-class/session capacity (`EntryCap`) — that's capacity-planning territory for the
financial-model-replacement app, not something the people hub's roster/permission needs require.

**registrations** — a participant's registration for one session + class (Clubspot's own term —
matched here rather than "enrollment"). This is deliberately at Clubspot's finest grain, its
`RegistrationCampSession` join ("Session Join Id" in the existing `ParticipantsReport`) rather than
its parent `Registration` object: a single Clubspot registration spanning multiple weeks/classes
becomes multiple rows here, one per session+class, matching what the current spreadsheet already
does. Billing/payment (Clubspot's `billing_registration`) stays out of scope, same as the rest of
the financial model.

| Field                       | Type                                        | Notes                                                       |
| ---------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`                        | uuid                                        | primary key                                                 |
| `person_id`                 | uuid, FK -> `people.id`                     | the participant                                             |
| `session_id`                | uuid, FK -> `sessions.id`                   |                                                              |
| `class_id`                  | uuid, FK -> `classes.id`                    |                                                              |
| `status`                    | enum (`confirmed`, `waitlist`, `cancelled`) | same vocabulary as #60; the *current* status — see [Change tracking](#change-tracking) for history |
| `clubspot_registration_id`  | string, nullable                            | groups rows from the same parent Clubspot registration (a multi-session signup); **not unique alone** |
| `clubspot_session_join_id`  | string, nullable, unique                    | the true per-row dedup key for #70 (`RegistrationCampSession`'s own id) |

### Change tracking

Registration status isn't a fact that just happens once — a row moves waitlist → confirmed →
cancelled, and knowing *when* matters (for reporting, and because Clubspot itself already tracks
it: `RegistrationCampSession.waitlist_updates` is a timestamped array of status changes on their
side). A flat `status` column loses that the moment #70 overwrites it. So:

- **`registration_status_events`** — append-only, one row per status transition.

  | Field               | Type                                         | Notes                                             |
  | -------------------- | --------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
  | `id`                | uuid                                         | primary key                                       |
  | `registration_id`   | uuid, FK -> `registrations.id`               |                                                    |
  | `status`            | enum (`confirmed`, `waitlist`, `cancelled`)  |                                                    |
  | `changed_at`        | timestamp                                    | when the status actually changed, per Clubspot's own `waitlist_updates`/`confirmed_at` |
  | `recorded_at`       | timestamp, default now()                     | when #70's sync wrote this row (may lag `changed_at` if sync polls infrequently) |

  #70 should backfill this from Clubspot's own history (`waitlist_updates`, `confirmed_at`) rather
  than only logging transitions it happens to observe between polls — Clubspot already did the hard
  part. `registrations.status` stays as the current-value cache every other collection joins
  against; this table is where the history lives.

### Data provenance

People data is an aggregation, not a source: `people.email`/`phone` are collected from whatever a
registration's contact form said, and the same real person can supply different values on different
registrations (a guardian re-registers a second child two years later with a new email address).
Confirmed by looking at the actual participants spreadsheet (the thing #70/#95 replace): it's a
fully-rebuilt-every-run flat snapshot with **no timestamp or version on any row today** — there's
nothing to tell a conflicting value apart from a stale one, or to say which registration a person's
current email came from.

- **`person_field_history`** — append-only, one row per observed value.

  | Field                    | Type                                              | Notes                                  |
  | ------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
  | `id`                     | uuid                                              | primary key                            |
  | `person_id`              | uuid, FK -> `people.id`                          |                                         |
  | `field`                  | enum (`email`, `phone`, `first_name`, `last_name`) | which `people` field this observation is for |
  | `value`                  | string                                            |                                         |
  | `source_registration_id` | uuid, FK -> `registrations.id`, nullable          | null if a staff member entered/corrected it directly in Directus instead |
  | `observed_at`            | timestamp                                        | the registration's own date — when this value was actually submitted |
  | `recorded_at`            | timestamp, default now()                          | when #70's sync wrote this row |

  `people.email`/`phone`/`first_name`/`last_name` stay as the current-value cache (#70 updates them
  to whichever source has the latest `observed_at`); this table is the audit trail behind them, and
  what a staff member would open to resolve "which of these two emails on file is right."

| `clubspot_camp_id`  | string, nullable, unique | dedup key for #70                              |

**sessions** — a dated instance of a program (Clubspot's `CampSession`).

| Field                    | Type                      | Notes             |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------- | ----------------- |
| `id`                     | uuid                      | primary key       |
| `program_id`             | uuid, FK -> `programs.id` |                   |
| `start_date`, `end_date` | date                      |                   |
| `clubspot_session_id`    | string, nullable, unique  | dedup key for #70 |

**classes** — an age/skill subdivision within a program (Clubspot's `CampClass`, e.g. "Beginner" vs.
"Advanced"). Modeled now, not deferred: a registration is for a specific session *and* class, and
#70's sync needs somewhere to put that — see `registrations` below.

| Field                | Type                      | Notes             |
| --------------------- | ------------------------- | ----------------- |
| `id`                  | uuid                      | primary key       |
| `program_id`          | uuid, FK -> `programs.id` | a class belongs to the program, independent of which sessions offer it |
| `name`                | string                   |                   |
| `clubspot_class_id`   | string, nullable, unique | dedup key for #70 |

Not modeled: which classes a given session offers (Clubspot's `CampSession.campClassesArray`) or
per-class/session capacity (`EntryCap`) — that's capacity-planning territory for the
financial-model-replacement app, not something the people hub's roster/permission needs require.

**registrations** — a participant's registration for one session + class (Clubspot's own term —
matched here rather than "enrollment"). This is deliberately at Clubspot's finest grain, its
`RegistrationCampSession` join ("Session Join Id" in the existing `ParticipantsReport`) rather than
its parent `Registration` object: a single Clubspot registration spanning multiple weeks/classes
becomes multiple rows here, one per session+class, matching what the current spreadsheet already
does. Billing/payment (Clubspot's `billing_registration`) stays out of scope, same as the rest of
the financial model.

| Field                       | Type                                        | Notes                                                       |
| ---------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`                        | uuid                                        | primary key                                                 |
| `person_id`                 | uuid, FK -> `people.id`                     | the participant                                             |
| `session_id`                | uuid, FK -> `sessions.id`                   |                                                              |
| `class_id`                  | uuid, FK -> `classes.id`                    |                                                              |
| `status`                    | enum (`confirmed`, `waitlist`, `cancelled`) | same vocabulary as #60; the *current* status — see [Change tracking](#change-tracking) for history |
| `clubspot_registration_id`  | string, nullable                            | groups rows from the same parent Clubspot registration (a multi-session signup); **not unique alone** |
| `clubspot_session_join_id`  | string, nullable, unique                    | the true per-row dedup key for #70 (`RegistrationCampSession`'s own id) |

### Change tracking

Registration status isn't a fact that just happens once — a row moves waitlist → confirmed →
cancelled, and knowing *when* matters (for reporting, and because Clubspot itself already tracks
it: `RegistrationCampSession.waitlist_updates` is a timestamped array of status changes on their
side). A flat `status` column loses that the moment #70 overwrites it. So:

- **`registration_status_events`** — append-only, one row per status transition.

  | Field               | Type                                         | Notes                                             |
  | -------------------- | --------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
  | `id`                | uuid                                         | primary key                                       |
  | `registration_id`   | uuid, FK -> `registrations.id`               |                                                    |
  | `status`            | enum (`confirmed`, `waitlist`, `cancelled`)  |                                                    |
  | `changed_at`        | timestamp                                    | when the status actually changed, per Clubspot's own `waitlist_updates`/`confirmed_at` |
  | `recorded_at`       | timestamp, default now()                     | when #70's sync wrote this row (may lag `changed_at` if sync polls infrequently) |

  #70 should backfill this from Clubspot's own history (`waitlist_updates`, `confirmed_at`) rather
  than only logging transitions it happens to observe between polls — Clubspot already did the hard
  part. `registrations.status` stays as the current-value cache every other collection joins
  against; this table is where the history lives.

### Data provenance

People data is an aggregation, not a source: `people.email`/`phone` are collected from whatever a
registration's contact form said, and the same real person can supply different values on different
registrations (a guardian re-registers a second child two years later with a new email address).
Confirmed by looking at the actual participants spreadsheet (the thing #70/#95 replace): it's a
fully-rebuilt-every-run flat snapshot with **no timestamp or version on any row today** — there's
nothing to tell a conflicting value apart from a stale one, or to say which registration a person's
current email came from.

- **`person_field_history`** — append-only, one row per observed value.

  | Field                    | Type                                              | Notes                                  |
  | ------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
  | `id`                     | uuid                                              | primary key                            |
  | `person_id`              | uuid, FK -> `people.id`                          |                                         |
  | `field`                  | enum (`email`, `phone`, `first_name`, `last_name`) | which `people` field this observation is for |
  | `value`                  | string                                            |                                         |
  | `source_registration_id` | uuid, FK -> `registrations.id`, nullable          | null if a staff member entered/corrected it directly in Directus instead |
  | `observed_at`            | timestamp                                        | the registration's own date — when this value was actually submitted |
  | `recorded_at`            | timestamp, default now()                          | when #70's sync wrote this row |

  `people.email`/`phone`/`first_name`/`last_name` stay as the current-value cache (#70 updates them
  to whichever source has the latest `observed_at`); this table is the audit trail behind them, and
  what a staff member would open to resolve "which of these two emails on file is right."

  Considered one polymorphic history table shared between this and `registration_status_events`
  (same shape: value + source + timestamps) — kept them separate instead. Two small, plainly-typed
  tables are easier to write permission filters against (e.g. a Guardian's own-minor scope) than one
  generic table needing a many-to-any relation to know what it's a history *of*.

5	## People hub: schema and permission model
6	
7	Design doc for the Directus data model behind Layer 2 of `docs/architecture.md` (the CRM / people
8	hub), per the plan agreed on issue #69. Covers the collections, fields, and permission policies;
9	deployment and rollout are tracked in the sibling issues (#92-#95) that decompose #69.
10	
11	### Scope and non-goals
12	
13	- Models what Clubspot actually gives us: people, their guardian/emergency-contact relationships,
14	  programs/sessions, and registrations. No household grouping — Clubspot has no concept of a
15	  household, only per-registration guardians and emergency contacts, so that's what the schema keys
16	  off.
17	- Terminology matches Clubspot and the website: **program** (Clubspot's `Camp`), **session**
18	  (`CampSession`), **registration** (`Registration`) — not "enrollment." Clubspot's **class**
19	  (`CampClass`) concept is named for, but not modeled by, this schema — see the `programs`/`sessions`
20	  note below.
21	- Auth identity is deliberately separate from person data — see [Auth identity](#auth-identity)
22	  below.
23	- Coach and guardian **portals** (thin clients calling this API) are out of scope; this doc defines
24	  the roles/policies they'll eventually use, but nothing here provisions their logins. That's #65.
25	
26	### Collections
27	
28	**people** — one row per human known to the org: staff, coaches, guardians, participants, emergency
29	contacts. Roles aren't stored — they're derived from relationships: staff from `directus_user_id` +
30	Directus role, coach from an `event_staff` row, guardian/emergency contact from a `contacts` row,
31	participant from a `registrations` row.
32	
33	No `clubspot_id` here. Clubspot has no stable person record — each registration carries its own
34	contact data, and one real person can show up as the contact on many registrations. Deduplicating
35	and collecting those into a single `people` row (by email, most likely) is the identity-resolution
36	problem #70's sync has to solve; it isn't a field this schema can just copy in.

45	
46	**medical_profiles** — one-to-one with `people`, kept as its own collection so its permission policy
47	can be stricter than a roster-level `people` read (allergies, medications, conditions, physician
48	contact).

51	| ---------------------------------------- | --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
52	| `person_id`                              | uuid, PK, FK -> `people.id` | one profile per person, so `person_id` is the key |
53	| `allergies`, `medications`, `conditions` | text                        | free-form                                         |
54	| `physician_name`, `physician_phone`      | string, nullable            |                                                   |
55	
56	**contacts** — one join collection for both relationship kinds Clubspot gives us (guardian and
57	emergency contact), rather than a separate table per type, since the shape is identical. Other
58	relationship kinds, if they're ever needed, get their own dedicated table rather than growing this
59	one's `relationship_type` enum.

61	Like `people`, these rows have no Clubspot id of their own to key off — Clubspot doesn't model a
62	guardian/emergency contact as a linked record, just flat strings on the participant
63	(`parentGuardianName`/`_secondary`, `emergencyContact`/`emergencyRelationship`). `contact_order`
